summary: Civilian Conservation Corps fire observation tower at the peak of Trail Ridge beside US 82 in Brantley County; unmanned late in the 20th century.

access.note: Beside U.S. 82 and visible from the road. No source names the owner or says the tower is open to climb; do not climb unless that is confirmed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Digital Library of Georgia places the tower three miles west of Hoboken; the marker database places the marker 0.4 miles west of Petty Crossing Road on U.S. 82. The story reports both. The marker database's coordinates match this record's point.

sources.title: Fire Tower @ Trail Ridge; US 82; Brantley County, GA

notes_for_editor: The build date comes from one local history page (The GAGenWeb Project, Brantley County) that gives only 'late 1930's'. The record has no built event: the 1937 year was a placeholder with no documented source, so it was removed and the story gives only 'late 1930s'. Check Civilian Conservation Corps or Georgia Forestry Commission records before adding a year. Location: the Digital Library of Georgia gives coordinates 31.18106, -82.13484, about 5 km west of the marker database point (31° 11.364′ N, 82° 4.799′ W), which matches this record. Elevation: the 2016 tower table gives 135 ft; the marker says the ridge top is about 160 ft and the local history says 100 ft. Not used. Unverified lead: a search-result snippet from a Brantley County History Facebook post (the page could not be read) mentions a Highway 82 fire in April 2026. No readable source says it reached the tower; check before publishing condition. Possible photo: Wikimedia Commons file by DanTD, CC BY-SA 4.0, dated 29 December 2022; not added because the direct image URL was not read. Ownership and climb status are unknown.
